lanes.summary: GH-3149 adds an exact kd-tree/ball-tree/brute-force neighbor index and rewires KNN, DBSCAN and LOF to query through it. I read the full 2603-line brief (ticket, receipt, and the complete diff for neighbors/{mod,kd_tree,ball_tree,brute,metric,tests,tests_rewire,kani_proofs}.rs plus the gaussian_nb.rs/dbscan.rs/lof.rs rewires). The pruning bounds are sound (kd single-coordinate lower bound valid for p>=1/Manhattan/Chebyshev; ball triangle-inequality bound with a slack term that only ever widens the search, never narrows it), tie-breaking is a pure (distance, index) order independent of tree shape, and the exactness/radius/sublinear/degenerate/metric-axiom proptests match their stated bounds. The one disclosed deviation — distance-weighted KNN predict_proba held to 1e-6 instead of bit-identical, because the old code summed 1/d in an unspecified select_nth_unstable partition order — is legitimate: the ticket's "identical labels/scores" criterion is satisfied exactly (DBSCAN labels, LOF scores/predict, KNN predict and unweighted proba are all bit-identical per the 153/180 exact pinned digests), and the 27 weighted-proba rows are gated by both a legacy-reference reproduction check and a 1e-6 bound, so the test can still fail. The re-measured kd-tree mutation (split value + 0.5) turns 3 of the 6 exactness tests RED, consistent with the receipt. No unwrap()/panic added; the one non-test `.expect` in lof.rs is argued unreachable (Euclidean+Auto is never refused) and that argument holds given `is_tree_compatible`.

findings.claim: The roadmap entry (and roadmap.yaml) records GH-3149 as status: inprogress, progress 0%, with every acceptance-criteria checkbox unchecked ('[ ]'), while the implementation receipt in the same diff declares status: complete and marks every one of those same criteria MET. This is a bookkeeping inconsistency, not a code defect, but it means anyone reading the roadmap alone would not see the ticket as done.

This is a change from undefined to defined behavior, explicitly disclosed and tested. No refutations found.
